data.narrative:
Foxglove, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Adrian Macneil and Roman Shtylman, has raised $58M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable, all operating in Robotics & Manufacturing at Series B or Series C stages. Top private peers include Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $58M raised-to-date proxy, implying a $110M valuation. The Peer-Median method references a cohort of four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), Hadrian ($1.6B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—yielding a median valuation of $1.6B and a range of $1.0B to $1.8B.

The two methods produce materially divergent signals. Triangulation across both approaches supports a valuation range of $94M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $868M. The wide spread reflects tension between the stage-progression anchor based on historical raise activity and peer multiples, which command significantly higher valuations. Key uncertainties include the capital intensity and growth trajectory relative to the selected peer set, and the applicability of later-stage comparables to a current Series B position.
